existing_tips: Accusative: 'der Mann' becomes 'den Mann' – only masculine articles change in accusative.
Dative: 'helfen' always takes dative object – 'ihrer Mutter'.
Separable prefix 'aus-': 'ge-' goes between prefix and stem – aus·ge·lesen.
'Einen' is the accusative of 'ein' for masculine nouns.
'Stammtisch' is a German tradition – a regular table at a pub for a group of friends.
Accusative: 'sein' becomes 'seinen' for masculine – possessives follow 'ein' pattern.
The prefix at the end signals a separable verb – in main clauses, the prefix splits off and goes to
'dem alten' = dative masc.; adj. takes '-en' after definite article.
The indirect object (receiver) goes in dative. ich gebe dem Mann das Buch. Dem Mann = to the man. En
'Das Schloss' stays 'das' in accusative – neuter articles don't change.
